'''Gieve Patel''' (18 August 1940 – 3 November 2023) was an Indian poet, playwright, painter, as well as a physician.<ref>{{cite news |title=Art in Review; Gieve Patel and Sudhir Patwardhan|author=Holland Cotter |authorlink=Holland Cotter|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/02/24/arts/art-in-review-gieve-patel-and-sudhir-patwardhan.html |work=The New York Times |date= 24 February 2006 |access-date=1 February 2013}}</ref> He belonged to a group of writers who had subscribed themselves to the ''Green Movement'' which was involved in an effort to protect the environment. His poems speak of deep concerns for nature and expose man's cruelty to it. His notable poems include, ''How Do You Withstand'' (1966), ''Body'' (1976), ''Mirrored Mirroring'' (1991) and ''On killing a tree''. He also wrote three plays, titled ''Princes'' (1971), ''Savaksa'' (1982) and ''Mr. Behram'' (1987).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gieve Patel: Biography |url=https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?p=BIC&u=wikipedia&id=GALE%7CK1658000311&v=2.1&it=r&sid=bookmark-BIC&asid=b9840809 |access-date=23 August 2022 |website=Gale}}</ref>

Patel retired from his medical practice in 2005. He resided in Mumbai and was fully engaged in the art field. Patel was considered to be one of the important painters who portrayed the social reality parallel to the prominent painters of the Baroda School. Through his paintings, Patel explored contemporary life, with a focus on its complexity and beauty.<ref name=":0" /> He died from cancer in [[Pune]], on 3 November 2023, at the age of 83.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Gieve Patel, doctor and poet, passes away at 83 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/gieve-patel-doctor-and-poet-passes-away-at-83/articleshow/104957076.cms |work=The Times of India |date=4 November 2023 |access-date=4 November 2023 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Patel was born on 18 August 1940 in Bombay (now [[Mumbai]]).<ref>{{cite book |title=International Who's Who in Poetry 2004 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |year=2003 |page=255}}</ref> His father was a dentist and his mother was the daughter of a doctor.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Thayil|first=Jeet|title=60 Indian Poets|date=8 August 2008|publisher=Penguin Books Limited|isbn=978-93-5118-234-4|url=https://www.google.com/search?q=Thayil,+Jeet+(8+August+2008).+60+Indian+Poets.+Penguin+Books+Limited&tbm=bks|language=en}}</ref> He was educated at St. Xavier's High Schooling and [[Grant Medical College]], [[Mumbai]]. After becoming a doctor, he had initially worked in a government job in his native village of [[Nargol]] in southern [[Gujarat]]. He then continued his work as a general practitioner in Mumbai until his retirement in 2005.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pillai|first=Pooja|date=15 January 2017|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/lifestyle/art-and-culture/down-the-rabbit-hole-2/|title=Down the Rabbit Hole|work=[[The Indian Express]]|access-date=2 May 2022}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Poetry ===
Patel's poetical works include ''Poems,'' launched by [[Nissim Ezekiel]], followed by ''How Do You Withstand, Body and Mirrored Mirroring''. One common theme throughout his work is the relationship between his landowning family and the tribal [[Warli]]s that worked in their estate.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Mujumdar|first=Neha|url=https://www.thehindu.com/books/the-long-road/article3910810.ece|title=The long road|date=18 September 2012|work=The Hindu|access-date=20 April 2020|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

Patel conducted poetry workshops in [[Rishi Valley School]] for more than a decade, and edited a collection of poetry published in 2006.<ref>{{cite web |last=Subramaniam |first=Arundhathi |author-link=Arundhathi Subramaniam |date=1 December 2005 |title=The Poet as Profane Monk |url=http://india.poetryinternationalweb.org/piw_cms/cms/cms_module/index.php?obj_id=2696&x=1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070321015354/http://india.poetryinternationalweb.org/piw_cms/cms/cms_module/index.php?obj_id=2696&x=1 |archive-date=21 March 2007 |access-date=2 May 2022 |website=india.poetryinternationalweb.org}}</ref> His poetry is included in ''Anthology of Contemporary Indian Poetry'' (BigBridge, United States).<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthology of Contemporary Indian Poetry Edited by Menka Shivdasani |url=http://bigbridge.org/BB17/poetry/indianpoetryanthology/Gieve_Patel.html |accessdate=9 June 2016 |publisher=BigBridge.Org}}</ref> One of his Poems ''Licence'' from the collection ''How do you Withstand'' is included in the anthology ''Confronting Love'' edited by Arundhati Subramanyam and [[Jerry Pinto]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=Confronting love : poems |date=2005 |publisher=Penguin Books India |others=Jerry Pinto, Arundhathi Subramaniam |isbn=9780143032649 |location=New Delhi, India |oclc=1193400813}}</ref> He was also featured in the poetry anthology ''The Golden Treasure of Writers Workshop Poetry on a killing tree ''(2008) ed. by Rubana Huq and published by [[Writers Workshop (publisher)|Writers Workshop]], [[Kolkata|Calcutta]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mandal |first1=Somdatta |title=Rubana Huq, ed. The Golden Treasury of Writers Workshop Poetry. Review : ASIATIC, VOLUME 3, NUMBER 1, JUNE 2009 |url=https://journals.iium.edu.my/asiatic/index.php/AJELL/article/view/82/67 |journal=Asiatic: IIUM Journal of English Language and Literature |date=15 June 2009 |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=126–129 |publisher=journals.iium.edu.my |accessdate=4 September 2018}}</ref> Additionally, he translated poems of the 17th century [[Gujarati language|Gujarati]] poet [[Akha Bhagat|Akho]] into English.<ref>{{cite news |title=Picture of perfection |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/culture/picture-of-perfection/cid/508791 |access-date=2 May 2022 |work=The Telegraph |date=6 June 2010}}</ref>

==== Published works ====

*''How Do You Withstand, Body''. Clearing House, (1976 ).
*''Mirrored, Mirroring''. [[Oxford University Press]], 1991.

=== Art ===

==== Paintings ====
Patel’s paintings received public attention when he painted the ''Politician'' series in the late 1960s and early 1970s. After the ''Politician'' serie''s'', Patel's well-known artworks are his ''Railway Platform'' series. These paintings originated from his experiences of sitting on a bench in a suburban railway station and watching the trains arrive and depart. One interesting aspect about these paintings is that Patel does not paint a single person on the platform i.e., the platforms are completely devoid of people. This is the moment when one train arrives, the crowd leaves and the passengers of another train are yet to arrive. Even though the platforms are always crowded, one feels the painter's longing to find solitude in the chaos of the city through the serene images in his paintings.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Bahulkar |first=Suhas |title=Encyclopaedia visual art of Maharashtra : artists of the Bombay school and art institutions (late 18th to early 21st century) |date=2 March 2021 |publisher=Pundole Art Gallery |isbn=978-81-89010-11-9 |edition=1st |location=Mumbai |oclc=1242719488}}</ref>
[[File:The Letter Home by Gieve Patel.jpg|alt=A painting by Gieve Patel|thumb|''The Letter Home'' (2002) by Gieve Patel]]
A similar atmosphere of mystery and peace can be seen in other city-based images painted by Patel in the later period. ''Two men near a handcart'', ''Vegetable seller'', ''Bus stop, The Letter Home'' are some of his notable works. In these paintings one can see how the painter works on two different aspects at the same time. On one hand, the idea is to create engaging experiences through pictures, colours and shapes. Whereas, on the other hand, there are struggles of people in their daily lives and its{{clarify|date=November 2023}} relationship with the artist. Given his closeness to life and the increasing violence in society, Patel's paintings in the 1980s and 1990s often featured wounded people and images of the dead. They take a critical look at some of the terrible aspects of human nature and society as a whole with a fearless and neutral perspective.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=पटवर्धन |first=सुधीर |title=पटेल, गीव्ह गुस्ताद |trans-title=Patel, Gieve Gustad |url=https://maharashtranayak.in/pataela-gaivaha-gausataada |access-date=19 August 2022 |website=महाराष्ट्र नायक |language=mr}}</ref>

For his last twenty years or so, the subject that kept Patel preoccupied was the view of looking into a well. The wells in Patel's native village Nargol and its vicinity are not that deep. Most of the time, one can bend down and touch the water in the well. One can see the sky and clouds reflected in the water along with the surrounding mountains, trees and bushes. Patel painted a series based on these views of the well, titled ''Looking into a Well''. While these are considered to be paintings of nature, the act of looking at nature appeared to Patel like peering into his own mind. Thereby, he continued to paint in this quest of self-exploration.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |url=https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=File%3A%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0_%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B6_%E0%A4%96%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%A1_%E0%A5%AC_-_%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%83%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%BE.pdf&page=353 |title=शिल्पकार चरित्रकोश खंड ६ - दृश्यकला |publisher=साप्ताहिक विवेक, हिंदुस्थान प्रकाशन संस्था |year=2013 |editor-last=बहुळकर |editor-first=सुहास |edition=1st |location=मुंबई |pages=288–290 |language=mr |trans-title=Artists' Encyclopedia Vol. 6 - Visual Arts |editor-last2=घारे |editor-first2=दीपक}}</ref>

Patel held his first art show at Mumbai's [[Jehangir Art Gallery]] in 1966, and went on to have several major exhibitions in India and abroad. He participated in the Menton Biennale, France in 1976; ''India, Myth and Reality,'' Oxford in 1982; ''Contemporary Indian Art,'' [[Royal Academy]], [[London]] 1982. He also exhibited for Contemporary Indian Art, Grey Art Gallery, [[New York City]], 1985; [[Indian Art]] from the Herwitz collection [[Worcester Art Museum]], [[Massachusetts]], 1985 and ''Coups de Coeur'' [[Geneva]], 1987.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gieve Patel |url=https://www.saffronart.com/artists/gieve-patel |access-date=23 August 2022 |website=Saffronart}}</ref>

==== Sculptures ====
Patel held the first exhibition of his sculptures in 2010. His sculptures are broadly based on two themes. The story of [[Ekalavya]] in the [[Mahabharata]] is one of the subjects, where the narrative is centred on Eklavya's hand and broken thumb. Another theme is that of [[Daphne]] in [[Greek mythology]], where the beautiful Daphne transforms into a tree to escape the lust of the god [[Apollo]]. In these sculptures, Patel depicts the semi-transformed state of Daphne's body.<ref name=":2" />
